Read a small part of Graphviz's DOT language into a graph of nodes, edges and attributes, refusing malformed graphs, edges and attributes.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/dot-dsl) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: dot_dsl.nomi
//# Reads a small part of Graphviz's DOT language: an undirected `graph`
//# of nodes, edges and graph attributes, each of which may carry
//# attributes.

/// An attribute's value: a whole number, `true` or `false`, or text,
/// quoted or not.
pub enum Value {
    Number Int
    Flag Bool
    Text String
}

derive Equatable for Value

/// A graph: its nodes and edges, each with its attributes, and the graph's
/// own attributes. An edge is keyed by its two nodes in order, so `b -- a`
/// is the edge `#("a", "b")`.
pub struct Graph {
    nodes: Map<String, Map<String, Value>>
    edges: Map<#(String, String), Map<String, Value>>
    attrs: Map<String, Value>
}

/// Why a text is not a graph.
pub enum Error {
    InvalidGraph
    InvalidEdge
    InvalidAttribute
    NodeNameNotAlphanumeric
}

derive Equatable for Error

impl Display for Error {
    fn to_string(error: Error) -> String {
        case error {
            .InvalidGraph -> "invalid graph"
            .InvalidEdge -> "invalid edge"
            .InvalidAttribute -> "invalid attribute"
            .NodeNameNotAlphanumeric -> "node name must be alphanumeric"
        }
    }
}

/// One statement inside a graph's braces.
enum Statement {
    GraphAttributes Map<String, Value>
    Node {name: String, attributes: Map<String, Value>}
    Edges {names: List<String>, attributes: Map<String, Value>}
}

/// Reads `text`, a `graph { ... }` with one statement on each line between
/// the braces. A line that starts with `//` or `#` is a comment.
pub fn parse(text: String) -> Result<Graph, Error> {
    lines =
        String.lines(text)
        |> Iter.map(String.trim)
        |> Iter.filter(fn line -> line != "" and not is_comment(line))
        |> Iter.to_list()

    ["graph {", ..body, "}"] = lines else { return Err(.InvalidGraph) }

    statements = body |> Iter.map(statement) |> Result.collect()?

    empty: Graph = #{nodes: %{}, edges: %{}, attrs: %{}}

    Ok(Iter.reduce(statements, add, from: empty))
}

fn is_comment(line: String) -> Bool {
    String.starts_with(line, "//") or String.starts_with(line, "#")
}

/// Reads one statement, `subject [name=value, ...];`, where the subject is
/// a node, a chain of edges `a -- b -- c`, or nothing for the graph's own
/// attributes.
fn statement(line: String) -> Result<Statement, Error> {
    Some(line) = String.strip_suffix(line, ";") else { return Err(.InvalidGraph) }

    #(subject, attributes) = case String.split(line, "[") {
        [subject] ->
            #(subject, %{})

        [subject, list] -> {
            Some(inner) = String.strip_suffix(String.trim(list), "]") else {
                return Err(.InvalidAttribute)
            }

            #(subject, attributes_in(inner)?)
        }

        _ ->
            return Err(.InvalidAttribute)
    }

    case String.words(subject) {
        [] ->
            Ok(.GraphAttributes(attributes))

        [name] -> {
            if not is_alphanumeric(name) { return Err(.NodeNameNotAlphanumeric) }

            Ok(#Statement.Node{name, attributes})
        }

        words ->
            Ok(#Statement.Edges{names: edge_names(words)?, attributes})
    }
}

/// The attributes of `name=value, ...`, the text between a statement's
/// brackets.
fn attributes_in(list: String) -> Result<Map<String, Value>, Error> {
    String.split(list, ",")
    |> Iter.map(fn pair -> {
        case pair |> String.trim() |> String.split("=") {
            [name, value] when name != "" and value != "" -> Ok(#(name, value_of(value)))
            _ -> Err(Error.InvalidAttribute)
        }
    })
    |> Result.collect()?
    |> Iter.to_map()
    |> Ok()
}

/// The value written `text`: quoted text, a whole number, `true` or
/// `false`, or else unquoted text.
fn value_of(text: String) -> Value {
    quoted = String.strip_prefix(text, "\"") |> Maybe.flat_map(&String.strip_suffix(&1, "\""))

    case #(quoted, String.to_int(text), text) {
        #(Some(inner), _, _) -> .Text(inner)
        #(_, Some(number), _) -> .Number(number)
        #(_, _, "true") -> .Flag(True)
        #(_, _, "false") -> .Flag(False)
        _ -> .Text(text)
    }
}

/// The nodes of a chain of edges, `a -- b -- c`, written as words.
fn edge_names(words: List<String>) -> Result<List<String>, Error> {
    #(names, links) =
        words
        |> Iter.with_index()
        |> Iter.partition(fn #(index, _word) -> index % 2 == 0)

    names = names |> Iter.map(.1) |> Iter.to_list()

    valid = Iter.count(names) == Iter.count(links) + 1
        and Iter.all(links, fn #(_index, word) -> word == "--")
        and Iter.all(names, is_alphanumeric)

    if valid { Ok(names) } else { Err(.InvalidEdge) }
}

fn is_alphanumeric(name: String) -> Bool {
    String.to_codepoints(name) |> Iter.all(fn c -> Codepoint.is_letter(c) or Codepoint.is_digit(c))
}

/// `graph` with `statement`'s nodes, edges or attributes added. Attributes
/// given again for the same node, edge or graph replace those given before.
fn add(graph: Graph, statement: Statement) -> Graph {
    case statement {
        .GraphAttributes(attributes) ->
            #{..graph, attrs: Map.merge(graph.attrs, attributes)}

        #Statement.Node{name, attributes} ->
            #{..graph, nodes: with_attributes(graph.nodes, name, attributes)}

        #Statement.Edges{names, attributes} -> {
            nodes = Iter.reduce(names, fn nodes = graph.nodes, name -> {
                with_attributes(nodes, name, %{})
            })

            edges =
                names
                |> Iter.windows(2)
                |> Iter.reduce(fn edges = graph.edges, pair -> {
                    [a, b] = Iter.sort(pair) else { unreachable "a window of two holds two names" }

                    with_attributes(edges, #(a, b), attributes)
                })

            #{..graph, nodes, edges}
        }
    }
}

/// `entries` with `attributes` merged into those of `key`, which it gains
/// if it lacks it.
fn with_attributes<K>(
    entries: Map<K, Map<String, Value>>,
    key: K,
    attributes: Map<String, Value>,
) -> Map<K, Map<String, Value>> {
    Map.update(entries, key, %{}, &Map.merge(&1, attributes))
}

// FILE: dot_dsl_test.nomi
import {
    dot_dsl
    dot_dsl.Graph
}

test "parse" {
    cases = [
        #(
            "empty graph",
            """
                graph {
                }
                """,
            #Graph{nodes: %{}, edges: %{}, attrs: %{}},
        ),
        #(
            "graph with one node",
            """
                graph {
                    a;
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{"a" => %{}},
                edges: %{},
                attrs: %{},
            },
        ),
        #(
            "graph with one node with attribute",
            """
                graph {
                    a [color=green];
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{"a" => %{"color" => .Text("green")}},
                edges: %{},
                attrs: %{},
            },
        ),
        #(
            "graph with one edge",
            """
                graph {
                    a -- b;
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{"a" => %{}, "b" => %{}},
                edges: %{#("a", "b") => %{}},
                attrs: %{},
            },
        ),
        #(
            "graph with one attribute",
            """
                graph {
                    [foo=1];
                }
                """,
            #{nodes: %{}, edges: %{}, attrs: %{"foo" => .Number(1)}},
        ),
        #(
            "graph with comments",
            """
                graph {
                    // a C-like comment
                    # a shell-like comment
                    [foo=1];
                }
                """,
            #{nodes: %{}, edges: %{}, attrs: %{"foo" => .Number(1)}},
        ),
        #(
            "graph with nodes, edges, and attributes",
            """
                graph {
                    [foo=1];
                    [title="Testing Attrs"];
                    a [color=green];
                    b [label="Beta!"];
                    b -- c;
                    a -- b [color=blue];
                    [bar=true];
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{
                    "a" => %{"color" => .Text("green")},
                    "b" => %{"label" => .Text("Beta!")},
                    "c" => %{},
                },
                edges: %{#("a", "b") => %{"color" => .Text("blue")}, #("b", "c") => %{}},
                attrs: %{
                    "foo" => .Number(1),
                    "title" => .Text("Testing Attrs"),
                    "bar" => .Flag(True),
                },
            },
        ),
        #(
            "multiple edges on one line",
            """
                graph {
                    a -- b -- c -- d [style=dotted];
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{"a" => %{}, "b" => %{}, "c" => %{}, "d" => %{}},
                edges: %{
                    #("a", "b") => %{"style" => .Text("dotted")},
                    #("b", "c") => %{"style" => .Text("dotted")},
                    #("c", "d") => %{"style" => .Text("dotted")},
                },
                attrs: %{},
            },
        ),
        #(
            "only 1 edge between nodes",
            """
                graph {
                    a -- b;
                    a -- b;
                    b -- a [color=blue];
                }
                """,
            #{
                nodes: %{"a" => %{}, "b" => %{}},
                edges: %{#("a", "b") => %{"color" => .Text("blue")}},
                attrs: %{},
            },
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, expected), description {
        assert dot_dsl.parse(text) == Ok(expected)
    }
}

test "parse errors" {
    cases = [
        #(
            "malformed input",
            """
                graphical {
                }
                """,
            "invalid graph",
        ),
        #(
            "malformed edge",
            """
                graph {
                    a --;
                }
                """,
            "invalid edge",
        ),
        #(
            "malformed edge 2",
            """
                graph {
                    a b;
                }
                """,
            "invalid edge",
        ),
        #("invalid edge type", "graph {\n    a == b;\n} ", "invalid edge"),
        #(
            "multiple edges missing a node",
            """
                graph {
                    a -- b --;
                }
                """,
            "invalid edge",
        ),
        #(
            "multiple edges missing a connector",
            """
                graph {
                    a -- b c;
                }
                """,
            "invalid edge",
        ),
        #(
            "empty attribute",
            """
                graph {
                    a [];
                }
                """,
            "invalid attribute",
        ),
        #(
            "malformed attribute",
            """
                graph {
                    a [name];
                }
                """,
            "invalid attribute",
        ),
        #(
            "empty attribute name",
            """
                graph {
                    a [=value];
                }
                """,
            "invalid attribute",
        ),
        #(
            "non-alphanumeric node name",
            """
                graph {
                    ? [key=value];
                }
                """,
            "node name must be alphanumeric",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, expected), description {
        assert Err(error) = dot_dsl.parse(text)
        assert "${error}" == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Adapted: the description asks for an internal DSL, graph-building code written in the host language. The canonical data instead parses DOT text, and this port does that: `parse` reads the text into a `Graph` value. An internal DSL in Nomi would be plain constructor calls on immutable values, which leaves nothing for the canonical cases to check.
- A `Graph` is three maps: nodes by name, edges by their two node names in order (`#("a", "b")` for `b -- a`, so an edge given twice either way round is one edge), and the graph's own attributes. Attributes are a `Map<String, Value>`, written out: a `typealias` of a named type would only hide it.
- An attribute's `Value` is an enum of `Number`, `Flag` and `Text`, since the canonical attributes mix `1`, `true` and `"Testing Attrs"`. `value_of` tries them in order with one `case` over a tuple: quoted text, a whole number, `true` or `false`, then unquoted text (`color=green`).
- `parse` keeps the lines that are not empty or comments and takes them apart with `["graph {", ..body, "}"] = lines else { ... }`, so a text without both braces is `InvalidGraph`.
- Each line between the braces is one statement, read by `statement` into a private `Statement` enum: graph attributes, a node, or a chain of edges. The words of its subject decide which: none, one, or `a -- b -- ...`, checked by `edge_names` as names at even positions and `--` between them. `Result.collect` stops at the first bad line, and `add` folds the statements into the graph. Attributes given again for the same node, edge or graph are merged, the later value winning.
- The four canonical errors are an `Error` enum with an `impl Display` giving the canonical messages. The error cases assert the message, `"${error}"`, so the table reads as the canonical data does.
- The canonical inputs are lists of lines; each is a `"""` string here. "invalid edge type" ends its last line with a space, which would be invisible at the end of a `"""` line, so it is an ordinary string with `\n`.
- The cases are two `subtests` tables, the graphs and the errors, since they assert different things.
